title: Daniel Ernst Jablonski to Pál Ráday, enciphering drafts 1705 and 1706-07 (SBB Berlin, Nachl. Francke 11,2/15 and 11,2/16): key of the numeric syllabary rebuilt from the drafts and validated on a held-out draft

steps.what: 350 figure/plaintext pairs (1,368 groups) from 11,2/15 nos 8, 13, 33 and 11,2/16 no 42 (pairs.tsv).
Key rebuilt from the pairs only (iterated segmentation, then corrections along the alphabetical order), 213 groups; frozen by SHA-256 with the protocol before the held-out draft was transcribed.

One measurement on 11,2/16 no 44 (scans 91-92, 541 groups transcribed blind from red-ink-only renderings, Latin read after the decode was frozen): 0.930 of characters against 0.247 for the best of 200 shuffled keys (mean 0.198); margin 0.683; thresholds >= 0.85 and margin >= 0.30, fixed in advance.

The received letter of 3 Aug 1705 (Wikimedia Commons scan from Révay 1974): its groups and Ráday's glosses agree with the key (191 ra, 208 vi, 203 ti, 170 o, 'bello gallico', 'armorum', 'principes'). Checked, not measured.
The two unglossed runs quoted on scan 72 from Ráday's letter ('ex aliena Cifra', 25 groups) do not read with this key.

Integration check (Daniel Bourdeau's session, PR #385): frozen/scripts/measure.py re-run on frozen/03_KEY.json, frozen/04_TRANSCRIPTION.txt and frozen/06_CLEAR.txt; SHA-256 of every frozen file recomputed against frozen/HASHES.txt. Confirmed: accuracy 0.9296 (958 decoded / 952 reference letters), best of 200 shuffled keys 0.2468, mean 0.1975, PASS; all seven hashes match.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was learned from the Latin written under the numbers in Jablonski's enciphering drafts (11,2/15 nos 8, 13, 33; 11,2/16 no 42) and validated once on a held-out draft (11,2/16 no 44). The content is the drafts' own (existing); the key is the contribution.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): protocol (frozen/01_PREREG.md) and key (frozen/03_KEY.json) hashed before the held-out draft 11,2/16 no 44 (scans 91-92) was transcribed; 541 groups transcribed blind; one measurement: 0.930 of characters (958 decoded / 952 reference letters) vs best of 200 shuffled keys 0.247 (mean 0.198), margin 0.683. Thresholds fixed in advance: >= 0.85 and margin >= 0.30. The script also folds w->u, y->i (not named in the protocol; declared). Key not changed after the measurement.

texts.label: Training drafts (11,2/15 nos 8, 13, 33, 1705; 11,2/16 no 42, 1706): 350 figure/plaintext pairs
texts.summary: The number groups of four enciphering drafts with the Latin words Jablonski wrote under them, the material the key was learnt from: Prussian mediation between Rákóczi's Hungarians and the Emperor in 1705-06.
texts.note: A table of figure groups and the plaintext written under each (scan, Latin as written, groups, note); the clear text between the enciphered words is not transcribed. Shown as the key's training material, not as a reading.

texts.label: 11,2/16 no 44, 14 Feb 1707, scans 91-92: the 541 held-out groups
texts.summary: Ilgen, in the King of Prussia's name, urges the Hungarians to make peace with the Emperor before the coming Franco-Imperial peace frees the Emperor's armies; P.S. on two casks of noble wine from Ráday passed on to the King, and on sending more via Cracow or Breslau.
texts.note: The enciphered runs of the draft (the clear words between them are not part of the portion). Decode with the frozen key, word-divided, beside the Latin Jablonski wrote under the groups; the draft's Latin is the plaintext of the time.

reading_review.note: decode read as Latin sentences against the draft's Latin; agrees except 8 words with a hole (9 groups illegible or outside the key) and clerk's slips (paax, grandm, uile, exse, notu li; 225 imperator for Caesar); raw decode unspaced, word-divided and normalised in reading.md; one reader

outcome.notes: The drafts carry their own plaintext, so we claim no reading and no solution; what is new is the key as a reusable table, rebuilt from 350 pairs and validated on a held-out draft. Révay 1974, which reproduces the received letter of 3 Aug 1705, could not be checked for a printed key.

prior.where: The drafts carry Jablonski's own Latin under the numbers (Daniel Bourdeau's leads review c26, 4 Nov 2026: leads 2169/2170 'read', key not built). The received letter of 3 Aug 1705 (glossed by Ráday) is reproduced in Révay Zoltán, II. Rákóczi Ferenc és korának rejtjelezése (Budapest, MNHF, 1974; Wikimedia Commons scan); whether Révay prints the key could not be checked (no open text found, 10 Nov 2026). Benda, Levéltári Közlemények 25 (1954) cites a clavis for the Jablonski correspondence in the Ráday archive (not seen). No target, branch or PR on these drafts in this repository; R483 (rakoczi1711) is another system.

human: Daniel Bourdeau's SBB/Kalliope sweep found the drafts (leads 2168-2171) and his leads review c26 (4 Nov 2026) vetted them as 'read' (enciphering drafts). Brice Dudout set the rules (protocol and key frozen before a single held-out measurement, thresholds fixed in advance). AI agents transcribed, built the key, measured and wrote up. No human palaeographer checked the transcription.
